transcript:
Meeting Header: KeplerHealth vendor onboarding - contract, DPA, pricing & KMS path
Date/Time: 2025-07-31 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Marcus Holt (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (KeplerHealth - Procurement), Derrick Moore (KeplerHealth - Head of Security), Maya Patel (KeplerHealth - VP Eng)

Summary (auto): Procurement and security wanted a single readout to clarify who signs which MSA clauses, how the DPA handles EU data, and what the pricing looks like for a 6-week pilot with possibility to reserve capacity. Redwood team to provide SOC2 and DPA; SE to run egress & KMS preflight.

[00:00] Marcus (Redwood AE): Hey everybody, thanks for joining. I'm Marcus from Redwood, AE on the Kepler account. We wanted to go through the outstanding contractual bits and make sure procurement and security are aligned before you go to legal signoff.
[00:18] Sofia (Procurement): Thanks Marcus. We have a short list: MSA redlines, DPA clarifications around EU PHI, and need to see SLA thresholds with crediting. Also pricing — we need a clear path to show finance.
[00:32] Marcus: Totally. Priya from our solutions team is here to do the technical bits and Priya will cover KMS and the onboarding tech preflight.
[00:45] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all, quick hi. I'll try not to drown you in infra, but yeah, KMS options, network egress, and the dedicated vs hosted pricing tradeoffs are the big levers.
[00:58] Derrick (Head of Security): Morning. A few clarifying Q's: do you support customer-managed keys in a way that keeps plaintext out of your control plane? Also — audit logs, retention, and whether we can attest to key rotation schedule.
[01:14] Priya: Yes, we support a couple of modes: Redwood-managed KMS (we manage keys, keys in our HSM), or customer-managed KMS via a supported external KMS (bring-your-own-key) where Redwood never sees the raw keys. There are some operational differences — e.g., backup/restore and rotation handoffs.
[01:34] Derrick: Right. For Kepler we have to have key control and we prefer HSM-backed keys centrally managed by our KMS. We also need to understand whether tokens or request metadata leak PII in logs.
[01:46] Marcus: On the DPA side, our standard template has a data residency clause and logs retention. We'll share the DPA and SOC2, but if you need specific retention windows or subprocessor lists, we can annotate.
[01:58] Maya (VP Eng): Quick ops question: for the pilot we'd like a 99.9 uptime target with SLOs around p99 latency at 300ms for short-form responses. How do you map dedicated vs hosted for that?
[02:15] Priya: Short answer: Dedicated gives more predictable latency — we can allocate reserved GPU pools. Hosted API is faster to start but you can see variance. For p99 300ms it depends on model size and sequence length. We'll need to run sample loads.
[02:31] Marcus: And pricing wise you can go reserved capacity (monthly commit) or pay-as-you-go for pilot. We'll put both numbers in the workbook — reserved is cheaper at scale but requires commit.
[02:45] Sofia: For procurement we also need to see the billing contact and breakdown — e.g., token vs embedding units, and any egress cost.
[02:55] Marcus: Absolutely. The pricing workbook will break down token rates, embedding units, reserved discounts, and any egress fees we see on cloud carriers.

[05:12] (later in call) Priya: On the KMS technical side, if you choose BYOK we'll ask you to create a service principal with limited permission for encrypt/decrypt and rotation. We'll test through a staged preflight — not full traffic but simulated requests to validate key wrapping and latency.
[05:30] Derrick: What's the failure mode if keys are rotated unexpectedly? Do you have automatic fallback?
[05:38] Priya: We support key rollover workflows; if Redwood detects a key error, requests are rejected and we can fail to a fallback model variant that uses Redwood-managed keys if that's part of the policy. For Kepler we can scope non-fallback if you require strict BYOK.

[08:01] Sofia: On the MSA — there are three redlines our counsel insisted on: (1) liability cap at twox fees, (2) data deletion obligations within 30 days after termination, and (3) explicit subcontractor list / subprocessors.
[08:18] Marcus: We typically handle liability cap conversations case-by-case. Our standard is one-year fees but we can take that back. Data deletion 30 days is doable for user content, we'll confirm retention for logs and backups. Subprocessors — we'll provide a current list and update cadence.
[08:38] Maya: Also, question on audit rights — we need a SOC2 and a way to validate claims. Is there an option for a third-party audit or a read-only view of logs?
[08:50] Marcus: SOC2 report — yes, we'll share the attestation. For detailed audit access, that often goes through a SOC2 + occasional on-site options for large customers; we can propose a compliance package if you need more.

[12:05] (timestamped middle segment when discussing pricing) Marcus: So pricing - for a 6-week pilot, here's a sample path: three options — (A) Hosted pay-as-you-go with per-token pricing and burstable capacity; (B) Short-term reserved (4-8 week reserved pool) with small commit; (C) Dedicated trial under a credit-backed trial with minimal commit. We'll put concrete numbers but wanted to know which procurement route is easiest for you.
[12:25] Sofia: Finance prefers to avoid long-term committs for pilot. Option A or C — C sounds attractive if you can do a credit or trial credit.
[12:36] Marcus: We can do a pilot credit for C, but it usually requires a short business addendum — easier than a full reserved contract. We'll include a line item for pilot credits in the workbook.

[18:50] Priya: If we run bench tests for your expected traffic shape (mix of short chat and longer context), we can recommend quantized model variants that lower per-token cost while hitting latency SLOs. That will feed into the economics model.
[19:05] Maya: Perfect. We'll share a sample traffic profile and some benchmark prompts.

[25:22] Derrick: About the DPA: we need explicit language for EU PHI — Kepler works with EU partners and we must ensure data doesn't transit outside EU regions. Does Redwood support region pinning for both inference and control plane?
[25:38] Priya: We support region pinning for inference workloads on Private and Dedicated — hosted has region options but some control-plane metadata may be in other regions depending on your Private vs Hosted choice. For strict EU PHI you likely need Dedicated or Private deployment.
[25:55] Marcus: We'll mark that as a scoping item. If you need full EU residency for user content and logs, we'd push Private or Dedicated with customer-managed networking.

[32:10] Sofia: Procurement timeline — our procurement cycle needs vendor paperwork, a PO, and a pricing justification to C-level. We need to know if Redwood can accept net-60 payment terms on pilot or if finance needs net-30.
[32:26] Marcus: For pilot credits we can be flexible but for committed reserved pools finance usually expects net-30. We'll add both options in the workbook and highlight the financial ops path.

[38:00] (questions from Kepler legal) Maya: On indemnity and IP — typical question: does Redwood claim IP on derivative prompts or fine-tuned corp data?
[38:14] Marcus: Our MSA clarifies that customer prompts and outputs remain customer's IP. We won't claim ownership of customer data. For model improvements we have a provision that allows aggregated non-identifiable telemetry to improve service; we can carve out corp data if you want.
[38:30] Derrick: We will want a clause excluding PHI and proprietary corp prompts from any training telemetry.
[38:38] Marcus: Noted — we'll flag that redline in the annotated DPA/MSA we send.

[43:12] Priya: On implementation, the preflight will test connectivity to your VPC endpoints, and KMS rotations. We'll also run a small perf job to validate p99 latency numbers so the SRE team can sign off.
[43:28] Maya: Good. For the preflight, our SREs want logs for a 48-hour window and a summary report. Is that possible?
[43:36] Priya: Yes, we can provide a preflight report with traces and token-level cost breakdown for the run. We'll redact any PII in the example logs.

[48:45] Sofia: Okay recapping next steps: Redwood to send DPA and SOC2, pricing workbook with pilot and reserved options, and SE to run preflight scheduling. Kepler to provide KMS requirements doc and internal approver list.
[49:02] Marcus: Correct. We'll aim to send the annotated MSA and pricing workbook within 3 business days. Priya will propose preflight slots by EOD tomorrow.
[49:15] Derrick: One last item — can you confirm who at Redwood is the escalation contact for security incidents? We need a named contact for our vendor registry.
[49:25] Marcus: Yes, security escalation is Dana Reed (Security Ops) — I'll cc Dana on the DPA email and include phone + backup.
[49:40] Sofia: Great. Thanks everyone.
[49:47] Maya: Thanks. Looking forward to the preflight.
[50:05] Marcus: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the docs and action items.

(End of transcript)
